message.content:
Based on my search, here are the main ways to pay federal taxes online in the United States:

## 1. IRS Direct Pay
**Free service** that allows you to pay directly from your checking or savings account. No registration or enrollment is required, though you will need to verify your identity using information from a prior-year tax return. You can schedule payments up to 365 days in advance and modify or cancel payments until two business days before the scheduled date.

- Website: https://www.irs.gov/payments/direct-pay-with-bank-account
- Available: Monday–Saturday, midnight to 11:45 p.m. EST; Sunday, 7 a.m. to 11:45 p.m. EST

## 2. Electronic Federal Tax Payment System (EFTPS)
A **free, secure service** from the U.S. Treasury for both individuals and businesses. **Note:** EFTPS no longer accepts new enrollees as of 2025. Existing users can still use the system, but new users should use IRS Direct Pay or other options instead.

- Website: https://www.eftps.gov
- Features: Schedule payments up to a year in advance, 24/7 availability, comprehensive payment history

## 3. Electronic Funds Withdrawal (EFW)
Available when you **e-file your tax return** through tax preparation software or a tax professional. You authorize a direct debit from your bank account when filing. This is typically free (check with your bank for any fees).

## 4. Debit or Credit Card
You can pay online through **IRS-authorized third-party processors**:
- **Pay1040** (https://www.pay1040.com)
- **ACI Payments** (https://www.acipayments.com)

| Payment Type | Fee |
|-------------|-----|
| Debit card | ~$2.10–$2.15 flat fee |
| Credit card | 1.75%–1.85% of payment (minimum $2.50) |

Digital wallets like Venmo, PayPal, and Click to Pay may also be accepted.

## 5. IRS2Go Mobile App
The IRS's official mobile app (available for iOS and Android) lets you make payments via mobile-friendly versions of Direct Pay or by debit/credit card.

## Important Update: Electronic Payment Mandate
A March 2025 Executive Order requires most federal tax payments to be made **electronically starting after September 30, 2025**. Paper checks and money orders will no longer be accepted. Exceptions apply for individuals without banking access or in emergency situations.

## Other Options
- **IRS Online Account**: Manage and make payments through your personal IRS account
- **Same-day wire transfer**: Available through your bank
- **Cash payments**: Through PayNearMe at participating retail locations (must initiate online)

Sources:
1. https://fiscal.treasury.gov/payments-to-government/electronic-federal-tax-payment-system-eftps
2. https://www.nerdwallet.com/taxes/learn/pay-irs-options
3. https://www.zinnerco.com/zinner-blog/executive-order-requires-electronic-payment-of-federal-tax
4. https://www.tax1099.com/irs/irs-federal-tax-payment/
5. https://www.hrblock.com/tax-payment-center/
6. https://www.taxact.com/support/24794/2020/tax-due-payment-methods-federal-only
7. https://www.taxact.com/support/1142/2020/eftps-online-electronic-federal-tax-payment-system
8. https://www.wallstreetmojo.com/electronic-federal-tax-payment-system/
